::: {.callout-tip}
## The plan

- **Data:** CB reports from **challenging** rehearsals only: 66 trainees × 3 functions = 198 reports
- **Compare:** PR (demanding) vs NR (screaming, avoiding) vs AR (repetition)
- **Model:** a mixed model with a predictor that has **three** levels, plus the design variables
:::

| | CB | SH | PF |
|---|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| **challenging: PR, NR, AR** | ● | | |

```{webr}
#| caption: Setup
#| edit: false
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(lmerTest); library(ordinal); library(ggplot2) })
source("R/study_helpers.R")
d  <- load_affect()
ch <- subset(d, checkpoint == "child_behavior" & loop_type == "challenging")
ch$function_class <- factor(ch$function_class, levels = c("PR", "NR", "AR"))  # PR = comparison
```

## 1. Look at the data

```{webr}
#| caption: Average feelings for each function
#| fig-height: 5
feelings <- c(sam_feelings, ordinal_feelings)
avg <- do.call(rbind, lapply(feelings, function(v) group_means(ch, v, "function_class")))
avg$feeling <- factor(avg$feeling, levels = feelings)

ggplot(avg, aes(function_class, mean)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se), colour = "#d6604d") +
  facet_wrap(~ feeling, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Average rating (bars: 1 SE)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

The NR behavior (screaming, avoiding) stands out for **pleasure** and **dominance**.

## 2. The model for pleasure

With three groups, R picks one as the comparison (here PR) and gives a slope for each of the other two.

```{webr}
#| caption: Linear mixed model with three groups
m_pleasure <- lmer(pleasure ~ function_class + challenge_position + pb_order_group +
                     feedback_condition + (1 | participant_id), data = ch)
summary(m_pleasure)$coefficients
```

```{webr}
#| caption: What the three numbers mean
#| fig-height: 4.5
map_rq4(d, "pleasure")
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reminder: one intercept, one slope per other group

| Term | Value | Meaning here |
|------|-------|--------------|
| `(Intercept)` | 0.86 | Average pleasure for **PR** (the comparison group) |
| `function_classNR` | −1.21 | NR minus PR (p < .001) |
| `function_classAR` | +0.23 | AR minus PR (no clear difference) |
| `challenge_position1`, … | | Design variables: whether this was the 1st, 2nd or 3rd challenging rehearsal, the order group and the feedback style |

Each trainee saw each function only once, so the random part can only give each trainee their own intercept, `(1 | participant_id)`.
:::

**Do the three differ at all?** One overall test answers that:

```{webr}
#| caption: Overall test
anova(m_pleasure)
```

The `function_class` row is the overall test (p < .001). The other rows test the design variables.

**What about NR vs AR?** Make NR the comparison group and fit again:

```{webr}
#| caption: Change the comparison group
ch$function_NR <- relevel(ch$function_class, ref = "NR")
m_nr <- lmer(pleasure ~ function_NR + challenge_position + pb_order_group +
               feedback_condition + (1 | participant_id), data = ch)
summary(m_nr)$coefficients[1:3, ]
```

AR is 1.44 points more pleasant than NR (p < .001).

## 3. All six feelings

The ordinal models were fitted ahead of time. First the overall test for each feeling:

```{webr}
#| caption: Overall test per feeling
results <- load_results()
overall <- results[results$rq == "RQ4" & results$term == "overall", c("feeling", "p")]
overall$clear_difference <- ifelse(overall$p < 0.05, "yes", "no")
overall$p <- signif(overall$p, 2)
rownames(overall) <- NULL
overall
```

Then the NR comparisons, where most of the differences are:

```{webr}
#| caption: NR compared with PR and with AR
#| fig-height: 3
nr_vs_pr <- six_results(results, "RQ4", "function_classNR")
show_six(nr_vs_pr)
plot_six(nr_vs_pr, sam_label = "NR minus PR (SAM points)")

ar_vs_nr <- six_results(results, "RQ4", "function_NRAR")
show_six(ar_vs_nr)
plot_six(ar_vs_nr, sam_label = "AR minus NR (SAM points)")
```

## 4. What about order?

The three functions were shown in three different orders (`pb_order_group`), so each function appeared first, second or third equally often. The four versions of each comparison:

```{webr}
#| caption: NR minus PR, four versions
checks <- load_checks()
order_table(checks, "RQ4", "function_classNR")
```

```{webr}
#| caption: AR minus NR, four versions
order_table(checks, "RQ4", "function_NRAR")
```

The pleasure and dominance differences hold in every version. Arousal (NR vs PR) hovers around p = .05, so it isn't a clear result.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Three things to keep in mind

- **Many tests, a few false alarms.** We ran a lot of tests here. As in [Chapter 1](01-basics.qmd), a few p-values near .05 can appear by luck, so treat frustration (overall p = .044) and boredom (p = .023) with caution.
- **Boredom is rare.** Most boredom answers are "not at all", which makes its odds ratios huge and very uncertain (look at the wide intervals).
- **Function and task go together.** Each function was shown during a different teaching task (PR with tacting and labeling, NR with receptive instructions, AR with receptive expression). A difference could come from the task as well as the behavior.
:::

## Answer

::: {.callout-important}
## RQ4: How does trainees' affect differ across behaviors with different functions?

The **NR** behavior (screaming and avoiding, to escape the task) was the hardest for trainees:

- **least pleasant**: 1.2 points below PR and 1.4 below AR
- **least in control**: dominance about 0.5–0.6 points lower than for PR and AR

PR (demanding) and AR (repetition) felt about the same. Arousal and confusion did not clearly differ between the three. Frustration and boredom showed weak differences (NR higher than AR) that need caution.
:::

## Try it

Fit the pleasure model with **AR** as the comparison group. What is the PR minus AR difference?

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_rq4
#| autorun: false
ch$function_AR <- relevel(ch$function_class, ref = "______")
m_ar <- lmer(pleasure ~ function_AR + challenge_position + pb_order_group +
               feedback_condition + (1 | participant_id), data = ch)
summary(m_ar)$coefficients[1:3, ]
```

::: {.solution exercise="ex_rq4"}
Use `ref = "AR"`. PR minus AR is −0.23 (no clear difference), and NR minus AR is −1.44.
:::

## Summary of the whole study

| | Question | Short answer |
|---|----------|--------------|
| RQ1 | Challenging behavior | Worse feelings about the child: less pleasure and control, more arousal, confusion and frustration |
| RQ2 | Own handling | Much better than about the child: pleasure near baseline, control partly back, calmer, less confused |
| RQ3 | After feedback | The gaps shrank further for control and confusion |
| RQ4 | Different functions | NR (screaming, avoiding) was the least pleasant and gave the least sense of control |

How sure can we be? See [Model checks](10-model-checks.qmd).
